goals: Implement a repeatable `cliyard runtime-drill` diagnostic that runs readiness-timeout, verifier-command failure and cleanup-failure scenarios in three separate OS child processes. Add src/runtime/failure-drills.ts as the orchestrator/report layer and a child entry that creates isolated scratch control/worktree directories, starts real finite services with RuntimeManager or the shell Verifier, detects the expected rejection, and exits 0 only when the observed evidence matches. The readiness timeout case must skip verifyCommands; the verify failure case must preserve a non-zero exit code; the cleanup failure case must use an injected allocator release failure and persist cleanup=failed while never reporting acceptance. Every case must prove the service process is gone and its port is bindable afterward. Retain runtime manifests, logs, pid/pgid, lease count, command results and failure reasons under a gitignored output directory, and emit a versioned runtime-failure-drills.json report. Add a focused test that drives the public CLI/test seam and checks the report and artifacts. Add a disjoint runtime-failure-drills port pool to tests/test-port-ranges.ts, a package.json script, and top-level CLI/help wiring. Do not add dependencies.
nonGoals: No changes to reaper ownership rules
No browser, Playwright, screenshot or axe integration
No SQLite, cloud execution or admission scheduler
